our_title: Fixed-vertex merge hash table undersized: probe loop never ends (zero-load trigger fixed)
ran: cd $WORK/repro && ./runall.sh pristine|pristine64 (LD_LIBRARY_PATH=$INFRA/asan/lib, asan64): `gra01 64 0` -> 'ret=0 100 101 ...' (hung in 7.0.17), `gra01 32 0` and `gra01 300 0 1` -> ret=0. The original zero-load trigger is gone; but `PS3-G12-1/fewfix 1 64` -> killed by timeout 60 (rc 124), gdb: '#0 _SCOTCHkgraphMapRbVfloMerge (dfixmax=1, vfixnbr=1) at kgraph_map_rb.c:428' (see PS3-G12-1).
severity_note: Hang from the public API with legal input (zero-load fixed vertices are explicitly allowed: 'Vertex loads can be 0 if we have fixed vertices', library_graph_map.c:209). Same as review.
evidence: kgraph_map_rb.c:413-415: `for (hashmsk = 1; hashmsk < dfixmax; hashmsk = 2 * hashmsk + 1) ; hashmsk = hashmsk * 4 + 3; hashsiz = hashmsk + 1;`; :271-274 `if (veloval <= 0) continue; /* Do not create a slot for it */`; :423-436 inserts all `mappptr->domnnbr` existing domains before the fixed ones.
upstream_change: 22c9c42e Bugfix: make sure hash table does not fill up to capacity [report R. Perry]

upstream_fix_review.details: Right: kgraphMapRbVfloBuild no longer creates slots for zero-load fixed vertices (kgraph_map_rb.c:271-274) and its table is sized from dfixmax = min(vfixnbr, archsize) computed once in kgraphMapRb (:150-160), which bounds its entries; the int shift '1 << (hashsiz + 2)' is gone from both routines; the unused archptr parameter of VfloBuild is dropped. Wrong: kgraphMapRbVfloMerge (:413-415) is now sized from dfixmax ONLY, but it first inserts every domain of the mapping computed on the free vertices (:423-436, mappptr->domnnbr entries, up to the number of parts). 7.0.17 sized it from domnnbr + vflonbr. With fewer than ~domnnbr/4 distinct fixed terminals the table (minimum 8 slots) fills up and the probe loop has no exit: SCOTCH_graphMapFixed/graphPartFixed with 1 fixed vertex and >= 9 parts hangs (default strategy, through kgraphMapMl -> kgraphMapRb), 32/64-bit. The shipped tests only fix 4-12 vertices on small architectures, so they miss it. Minor: 'fariable-sized' typo in the comment at :151. See PS3-G12-1. Independently found by G25 as PS3-G25-1 (same hunk).
upstream_fix_review.compared_with_ours: Ours (7.0.17 0003) sized Merge from min(archsize, vfixnbr) + domnnbr and added a regression test (zero-load fixed vertices); his avoids zero-load slots in Build too (nicer: fewer slots) and factors dfixmax once, but drops the domnnbr term and adds no test. Rebased as 0002: keeps his structure, adds mappptr->domnnbr to the Merge bound, and the test now covers both the zero-load case and the single-fixed-vertex case (hangs on pristine 7.0.18 at kgraph_map_rb.c:428).

review_accuracy: Accurate, including the regime (distinct fixed terminals > 4 x next power of two of domnnbr).
first_pass_critique: Right on status and mechanism. Its preferred one-liner (domnnbr + vfixnbr) is correct but leaves the vflonbr parameter unused instead of removing it, and does not bound the table by the architecture size as kgraphMapRbVfloBuild() does (for a fixed-size architecture with 1M fixed vertices on 4 terminals it would allocate a 64 MB table). Its option 2 would pass vflonbr > 0 with vflotab == NULL into kgraphMapRbVfloSplit(), which dereferences vflotab: a crash. The hashtab leak it notes on the mapResize path is real and is fixed by the GRA-23 commit (single exit point).

extra_instances.quote: hashsiz = 1 << (hashsiz + 2); /* Fill hash table at 25% maximum */

fix_options.label: Add existing domains to the Merge bound (on top of 22c9c42e)
fix_options.summary: for (hashmsk = 1; hashmsk < (mappptr->domnnbr + dfixmax); ...) in kgraphMapRbVfloMerge; test_scotch_graph_map gains zero-load and single-fixed-vertex cases.
fix_options.tested: fewfix 1 64 / 4 64 / 1 1024 64 -> ret=0 (pristine: hang); gra01 kit unchanged; check_scotch_graph_map, check_prog_gmap, check_prog_gpart pass 32/64-bit; the new test hangs on pristine 7.0.18 (gdb in Merge, dfixmax=1).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Table up to 4x larger when many domains exist (transient, freed at once).
fix_options.maintainer_fit: One expression in his new loop; keeps his dfixmax factoring.

fix_options.summary: kgraphMapRb passes dfixmax + grafptr->m.domnnbr to Merge.
fix_options.tested: untested
fix_options.tradeoffs: Same effect; spreads the sizing logic across two routines.

our_title: Band graph anchors' old parts set for old domain count, not current one
ran: ./runall.sh pristine: `gra05 2 8 "$ST"` -> 'AddressSanitizer: SEGV ... #0 _SCOTCHarchCmpltDomIncl arch_cmplt.c:418 #1 kgraphMapFmPartAdd kgraph_map_fm.c:774'; 64-bit pristine ret=0 (memory-content dependent, as in 7.0.17); patched 32/64 -> ret=0; check_prog_gpart_remap (with the regression lines) passes 32/64.
severity_note: Crash or silent use of garbage old parts from the public remapping API whenever the new part count differs from the old one and a band method runs (default strategies above 10000 vertices). Same as review.
evidence:
kgraph_band.c:267: memSet (bandparotax + bandvertnbr - bandgrafptr->r.m.domnnbr, ~0, bandgrafptr->r.m.domnnbr * sizeof (Gnum)); /* Old parts of anchors are unspecified */
kgraph_band.c:222: mapInit2 (&bandgrafptr->r.m, ..., grafptr->r.m.domnnbr); -- old mapping's count; :199: bandvertnbr += domnnbr; -- anchors use the current count.
kgraph_map_fm.c:668-670: if ((parotax != NULL) && (parotax[oldvertnum] != -1)) ... domoptr = &grafptr->r.m.domntab[parotax[oldvertnum]]
review_accuracy: Accurate, fix line correct. 'With more old parts than new, the memSet overwrites ordinary band vertices' is right. The first pass's remark that it may also write before the array start would need more old domains than band vertices (anchors included), conceivable only for a tiny band graph remapped from many parts; the fix covers it anyway.
first_pass_critique: Right; diff identical to the sketch. It only tested the ASan build, where the crash depends on the 0xbe fill of the first 4096 bytes; it did not note that larger graphs fail silently rather than crash, nor add a test.

severity_note: Public API (SCOTCH_graphPartOvl) crash in release builds; needs a bipartition that leaves a part empty, which happens on small (sub)graphs with real strategies and always with 'z'. Same rating as the review.
review_accuracy: Accurate on the crash mechanism (spltnum = partval = 0, NULL parttax, uninitialised splttab[0].vertnbr). Its 'Fix:' line (call with 1) is incomplete: it stops the crash but leaves the terminal-domain case wrong (shown above with r{sep=(z|f)}). Making Rb3* return errors through revaptr is unnecessary: their only failure paths are debug-only parameter checks that cannot trigger once the call is right.
first_pass_critique: Status, method and reproducer right; the preferred option (one-token fix) was tested only with strategies for which the degenerate child bipartition happens to put everything in part 0, so the wrong-domain case was missed; option 2 (guard in callee) has the same hole and leaves the recursion bipartitioning a graph onto a single domain. The 'maintainer precedent' claimed (wgraphPartRb starts with fake part 1) supports calling with 1 but not the missing terminal case.

our_title: Overlap partition leaves separator vertices adjacent to no part in no part
severity_note: Silent wrong result (a vertex in no part) but only on tiny (sub)graphs: isolated vertices, or pendant/boundary vertices of induced subgraphs at the leaves of the recursion; the review's Low is right. Reachable with the default strategy on ordinary graphs (path 4 vertices / 4 parts), not only on edgeless graphs.
evidence: doc/src/scotch/s_l.tex:1177-1180: 'the load of every separator vertex is accounted for several times, in each of the parts it separates' -- a separator vertex with no neighbour in a part separates nothing and is counted nowhere (wgraph.c:203-221 wgraphCost adds a separator vertex's load only to neighbouring parts). wgraph_part_rb.c:449-454: grafptr->fronnbr = datadat.fronnbr; ... wgraphCost (grafptr) -- nothing removes such vertices.
review_accuracy: Behaviour accurately described but the lead only covers zero-degree vertices; the same loss happens to vertices isolated in an induced subgraph, or whose neighbours all became separator vertices at other recursion levels (path 4 vertices / 4 parts: vertices 0 and 1 are lost). Its 'Fix:' (vertex-separation strategies) is one of the options but would change nested-dissection orderings and not cover the multi-level case.
first_pass_critique: Preferred option (post-pass on zero-degree vertices only) does not fix 'path 4 4' (still lost=2, see alt/SEP-17-a); the lost condition is 'no neighbour in a part', not degree zero. Its option 2 ('assign them while gluing') is not compiled and cannot see cross-level losses. Option 3 (vgraph separators) is correctly flagged as large blast radius.

fix_options.label: Post-pass in wgraphPartRb: assign to the lightest part every separator vertex with no neighbour in a part (recommended)
fix_options.summary: New static wgraphPartRbFron() called after wgraphCost(): removes such vertices from the frontier, assigns them to the lightest part, updates compload/compsize/fronload incrementally (neighbouring separator vertices now separate that part too).
fix_options.tested: repro above; check_scotch_graph_part_ovl, check_prog_gpart_overlap on 32-bit, 64-bit and SCOTCH_DEBUG_ALL builds (wgraphCheck validates the updated loads).
fix_options.tradeoffs: Changes outputs only when lost vertices exist; O(sum of degrees of lost vertices and their neighbours). Choice of the lightest part ignores locality (a lost vertex may be far from its part); a 2-hop neighbourhood choice would be a refinement.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Local to the RB method that produces the situation, guarantees the documented model for every vertex, does not touch the vgraph separators used by orderings. Same 'fix-up after recursion' idea as kgraphMapRbVfloMerge().

fix_options.label: Post-pass on zero-degree vertices only (first pass)
fix_options.summary: Move isolated frontier vertices to the lightest part.
fix_options.tested: read and compared: misses subgraph-isolated vertices (path 4 4 keeps lost=2 on the recommended fix's test matrix reasoning: vertex 0 has degree 1).

fix_options.label: Fix at the source in vgraphSeparateGg: do not leave an isolated root in the separator
fix_options.summary: When growth stops for balance reasons and the current root has no neighbour, put it back in part 0.
fix_options.tested: untested: only one of several separator methods (FM, DF, BD, ML...), does not cover cross-level losses; changes ordering results.

test_added: none: the existing check inputs (m16x16, bump, 4-32 parts) do not produce lost vertices; a deterministic case would need a tiny graph data file (path of 4 vertices) which is not in the file's style; repro/SEP-17/lost.c is the check.

fix_options.label: Do not split the context when deterministic behaviour is wanted (recommended)
fix_options.summary: In kgraphMapRbPart2() and wgraphPartRb2(), read CONTEXTOPTIONNUMDETERMINISTIC and run the two sub-tasks in sequence within the same context when it is set, exactly like graphMatchInit() falls back to sequential matching.
fix_options.tested: determinism runs above (1 == 2 == 4 threads once combined with G08's GG fix; overlap path already 1 == 2 == 4 with this series alone); zero warnings on 32/64-bit; check_prog_gpart, check_prog_gpart_overlap, check_scotch_graph_map on 32/64/debug builds.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Deterministic mode loses the recursion-level parallelism (each sub-task still uses all threads of the context for its own threaded methods, which are sequential in deterministic mode anyway). Non-deterministic mode unchanged.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: Caller-side check with the exact idiom of graph_match.c:205-225 (common_context.c cannot include context.h: the option enum is libscotch-level). 'Document that deterministic needs >= 2 threads' is not an option: the documentation already promises 'for any number of threads' and 2 and 4 threads differ as well (the split recurses).

fix_options.label: Always derive the second sub-task's generator, even when running sequentially
fix_options.summary: Make contextThreadLaunchSplit() draw the second generator and run the two sub-tasks itself when the context has a single thread, so that the pseudo-random streams are identical for every thread count without losing parallelism.
fix_options.tested: untested: changes the results of every single-threaded run (COMMON_RANDOM_FIXED_SEED results change between versions), touches the common layer used by all callers, and still requires every threaded method to be thread-count independent.
fix_options.tradeoffs: Keeps parallelism in deterministic mode; larger behaviour change.
fix_options.maintainer_fit: A design change he may prefer for 7.1, not a 7.0.x bugfix.
